proposal: Fix the WP-243 coverage-contract false HIGH breach that fires every pipeline run through a mid-month FIFA international break. Add an optional `breaks` array (UTC date windows) to the authority.json contract block: during a known league-pause window the status is a new `break` verdict instead of `breached`, so the always-HIGH contract-breach signal is not raised while the competition legitimately is not playing. `months` covers whole calendar months and therefore cannot model a pause INSIDE a month; lowering minUpcoming does not help because during the break upcoming falls to 0 (PL) / 1 (Eliteserien). Code: scripts/lib/coverage-contracts.js (new `break` status via a fail-soft isWithinBreak helper) + authority.schema.json (`breaks` property, date-pattern-validated) + the 2026/27 FIFA windows seeded onto the football:premier-league and football:eliteserien contracts. Downstream is safe by construction: detect-coverage-gaps.js and build-port-report.js both filter strictly on status==="breached", so a `break` contract produces no gap and does not colour the G2 contracts port.
evidence: coverage-audit.json 2026-11-09 TOP sourceIssue (severity HIGH, NEW this run): 'WP-243 dekningskontrakt — PL + Eliteserien: 14-d-horisonten overgår fetcherens ~5–6-d look-ahead under midt-i-måneden FIFA-pause (STRUKTURELL MISCALIBRATION)'. Both football:premier-league (minUpcoming 6) and football:eliteserien (minUpcoming 2) fired HIGH contract-breach; coverage-critic TRIAGED BOTH AS FALSE (FIFA window 14.–17. nov, next rounds 21.–23. nov web-confirmed) and routed it explicitly to improve/self-repair.

The same sourceIssue states the impact and names the fix: 'Uten en fiks re-fyrer begge HIGH-brudd hver kjøring gjennom HELE landslagspausen (9.–~18. nov) og trener agentene til å ignorere contract-breach-signalet — akkurat G2-støyen WP-243-schemaet advarer mot.' Proposed option (a): 'modeller FIFA-landslagsvinduet i coverage-contracts (ikke mål brudd når forrige runde nettopp spilt + neste runde >fetcher-look-ahead unna)'. This PR implements exactly that.

coverage-audit.json gaps[0] and gaps[1] (PL + Eliteserien) both carry 'TRIAGERT SOM FALSKT BRUDD: landslagspause', recurrences 0 firstSeen today — the breach is brand new and will re-fire every run until ~18 Nov. The Eliteserien contract's OWN note already documents the precursor of this failure (minUpcoming was lowered 4→2 on 07.09 for the Sept break) — threshold tuning has already been tried and is insufficient for the mid-month November window where upcoming hits 0/1.

contract-breach is defined as ALWAYS high severity (CLAUDE.md: 'the one gap class defined as a broken promise in advance') and is the only signal feeding the port-report contracts port into G2 — so a recurring FALSE high breach is maximally corrosive: it is precisely the signal the schema warns must stay noise-free ('et falskt brudd koster agent-triage og G2-støy').

FIFA 2026/27 men's international match calendar windows verified across multiple sources (Spreadex 2026-27 international break dates; Wikipedia FIFA International Match Calendar): 21.09–06.10 2026 (merged Sep/Oct), 09.–17.11 2026, 22.–30.03 2027, 07.–15.06 2027. PL gets Sep/Oct+Nov+Mar (off-season in June); Eliteserien gets Sep/Oct+Nov+Jun (off-season in March).

Simulation against the live authority.json with an EMPTY board (worst case): 09.11 and 14.11 → both football contracts status 'break' (breached []); 25.11 (after the window) → both 'breached' — proving the window suppresses ONLY the documented pause and never masks a genuinely dark board. The fix is strictly safe for recall: outside break windows behaviour is byte-identical to today.

npm test: 88 files / 1550 tests pass (1546 → +4 new coverage-contracts cases covering break/outside-window/off-season-precedence/malformed-fail-soft). Leverages existing WP-243 machinery (config + a pure function), matching the improve bias 'sharpen what exists over adding machinery'. All paths non-protected (scripts/lib + scripts/config, not .github/workflows or hooks) → auto-merge-eligible.
expectedEffect: From this run on, a known FIFA international break no longer produces a false HIGH contract-breach gap for Premier League or Eliteserien: coverage-contracts.json reports status 'break' for those competitions during 09.–17.11 (and the other seeded windows), so coverage-critic/research stop spending triage on a non-gap and the port-report G2 contracts port stays green through the pause. A genuine mid-season dead fetcher OUTSIDE a break window still breaches exactly as before — the recall floor is unchanged.
howWeKnow: On the next pipeline run (today is inside the 09.–17.11 window), coverage-contracts.json should show football:premier-league and football:eliteserien with status 'break' (not 'breached'), detect-coverage-gaps.js should emit ZERO contract-breach gaps for them, and the port-report contracts port should be green. After the window ends (~18 Nov) the resumed rounds 21.–23. nov board on cadence and the contracts flip to 'met'. If a football contract ever shows 'break' while the league is actually playing (would mask a real breach), a break window is mis-dated and should be narrowed.
notes: Chose this over: (a) the winter/handball/golf/EL-ECL/CS2 structural sourceIssues — all real but all carry-forward MEDIUM/HIGH with no NEW firing signal this run, and the winter-contract half was already shipped by the 02.11 improve run (PR #474); (b) schedule tuning — usage green (week 13%, 0 amber/red hours), no cron change warranted; (c) the research-escalation allowed_bots breakage — a protected .github/workflows path CI agents may not author (tracked in open issue #430). The FIFA-break miscalibration is the ONE item that is both newly firing AND fully fixable in non-protected paths.

Deliberately modelled the documented cause (FIFA calendar windows) rather than a mechanical 'recent past events suppress the breach' heuristic: the latter cannot distinguish an international pause from a dead fetcher (both show recent-past + zero-future under retainLastGood) and would weaken the recall floor. Explicit windows change behaviour ONLY inside the pause and never mask a real breach outside it.

Windows are AI-maintained config: when the 2026/27 season rolls over, research/improve refresh the dates (the schema pattern-validates YYYY-MM-DD). If a season's windows go stale the contract degrades gracefully back to today's behaviour (false breaches resume) — no worse than the status quo, and self-evident from a re-firing false breach.
